New Year's Day.description: Marks the beginning of the Gregorian calendar year. Celebrated with fireworks, parties, and making resolutions for the upcoming year.
traditions: Countdown events (e.g., Times Square ball drop)
New Year's Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Martin Luther King Jr. Day.description: Honors the civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Observed on the third Monday of January each year.
Martin Luther King Jr. Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Presidents' Day.description: Originally established to honor George Washington, now commonly viewed as a celebration of all U.S. presidents.
traditions: Visits to presidential monuments and museums
Presidents' Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Memorial Day.description: Honors military personnel who died while serving in the United States Armed Forces. Observed on the last Monday of May.
traditions: National Moment of Remembrance at 3:00 p.m.
Flag placed at half-staff until noon
Memorial Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Juneteenth National Independence Day.description: Commemorates the emancipation of enslaved African Americans in the United States. Marks June 19, 1865, when Union troops arrived in Galveston, Texas with news of freedom.
traditions: Educational events about African American history
Juneteenth National Independence Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Independence Day.description: Celebrates the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776, declaring independence from Great Britain.
Independence Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Labor Day.description: Honors the American labor movement and the contributions of workers to the strength, prosperity, and well-being of the country. Observed on the first Monday of September.
Labor Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Columbus Day.description: Commemorates Christopher Columbus's arrival in the Americas on October 12, 1492. Also known as Indigenous Peoples' Day in many jurisdictions.
traditions: Recognition of Native American cultures (in areas observing Indigenous Peoples' Day)
Columbus Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Veterans Day.description: Honors military veterans who served in the United States Armed Forces. Observed on November 11th each year.
Veterans Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Thanksgiving Day.description: A day for giving thanks for the blessing of the harvest and of the preceding year. Observed on the fourth Thursday of November.
traditions: Traditional foods (turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, pie)
Thanksgiving Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources

Christmas Day.description: Celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ. Observed on December 25th each year.
Christmas Day.source: Adapted from Wikipedia and public domain sources
